extracted.intended_audience: OPM, federal agencies (HR/legal offices), agency counsel, labor organizations, federal employees and other stakeholders commenting on or implementing adverse action and personnel classification rules
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards governing which federal employees are covered by chapter 75 adverse-action procedural protections when positions move between the competitive and excepted services, and the definition and scope of the exception for positions of a "confidential, policy-determining, policy-making, or policy-advocating character."

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of "employee" for part 752 coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of part 752, an "employee" is an individual who has accrued adverse action rights by completing probation or a current continuous service requirement and who occupies a position moved from the competitive service into the excepted service, or from one excepted service schedule to another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The changes add language to provide that such an employee is covered by the regulatory requirements for removal, suspension for more than 14 days, reduction in grade or pay, or furlough for 30 days or less; this reflects statutory requirements that accrued procedural rights cannot be taken away by involuntary moves of the employee's position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of accrued rights on involuntary moves
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals who have fulfilled their probationary or trial period requirement or the durational requirements under 5 U.S.C. 7511 will retain the rights conferred by subchapter II if moved involuntarily from the competitive service to the excepted service or within the excepted service to a new excepted service schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retention applies unless specifically prohibited by law; OPM relies on statutory text, legislative history, and legal precedents (e.g., Roth) establishing that an employee with accrued rights involuntarily moved retains those rights while in that position or any subsequent position to which moved involuntarily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary relinquishment of rights
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee will relinquish accrued rights if the employee voluntarily seeks, accepts, and encumbers a position that explicitly results in a loss of, or different, rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation distinguishes voluntary from involuntary movements; absent voluntary movement, accrued rights established in statute cannot be taken from employees by involuntary movement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of retained rights after multiple involuntary moves
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee who is moved involuntarily more than once will retain any applicable status and civil service protections while the employee still occupies that position or any other position to which the employee is moved involuntarily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM revised §752.401(c)(3)-(c)(8) to replace language referencing a "similar position" with the words "any other position to which the employee is moved involuntarily" to prevent agencies from stripping rights via repeated involuntary moves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for positions of confidential/policy character (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Positions determined to be of a confidential, policy-determining, policy-making, or policy-advocating character are excepted from the chapter 75 protections described in subpart D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exclusion is recognized in 5 U.S.C. 7511(b)(2); OPM adds definitions and conforming regulatory language across parts (e.g., 213.3301, 302.101, 432.101, 451.302, 752.201, 752.401) to standardize usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion does not override previously accrued rights from involuntary moves
rubrics_metrics.description: The exclusion for positions of a confidential, policy-determining, policy-making, or policy-advocating character does not apply if the incumbent was moved involuntarily to such a position after accruing rights as delineated in §752.401(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM revised exclusion language (e.g., §752.201(c)(7), §752.401(d)(2)) to clarify that the exclusion is not applied to strip rights from an incumbent who had already accrued rights prior to an involuntary transfer into an excluded position.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPM's definitional reading of "confidential, policy-determining, policy-making, or policy-advocating"
rubrics_metrics.description: OPM defines these phrases to refer to positions exclusively associated with a noncareer political appointment—i.e., positions held by noncareer political appointees (traditionally Schedule C) that (a) involve close working relationships with the President, head of an agency, or other key appointed officials responsible for furthering presidential goals and policies, and (b) carry no expectation of continued employment beyond the presidential administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The definition is grounded in statutory text, traditional tools of statutory interpretation, and longstanding executive-branch practice and history; OPM adopts it to limit the exception to what historically has been a small class of political appointee positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent overbroad application to policy-related job titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Merely having an office or title with the word "policy" (e.g., "policy analyst," "policy implementation") is not determinative of being a confidential/policy position for purposes of the exception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM and commenters emphasize the need for a narrow delineation to avoid classifying mid- or lower-level career employees whose work touches on policy as excepted; the rule aims to prevent overbroad classifications that could strip career civil servants of rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical and statutory sources constrain interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: The meaning of the exception must be read consistent with long-standing executive branch usage, legislative history, and precedents, which have historically equated the phrase with political (Schedule C/noncareer) appointments and a small universe of positions (roughly 1,500 historically).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM cites history (Roosevelt, Brownlow Committee, Hoover Commissions, Executive Orders, congressional reports) and statutory examples across agencies to support the understanding that the phrase refers to political appointees and should be narrowly applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conforming regulatory edits and standardization requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Conforming changes will be made across multiple regulations (e.g., 5 CFR 213.3301, 302.101, 432.101, 451.302, 752.201, 752.401) to standardize phrasing used to describe confidential/policy positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM is adopting regulatory definitions and will align language across parts to make explicit its interpretation of the exception in 5 U.S.C. 7511(b)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of SES positions (no expansion to SES)
rubrics_metrics.description: This rule addresses the competitive and excepted services and does not modify rules governing the Senior Executive Service (SES); the SES is governed by its own statute and adverse action procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although SES employees may have policy duties, the exception under 5 U.S.C. 7511(b)(2) and the OPM definition do not alter SES protections; OPM will not revise the rule to add SES employees to these provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revisions reflecting repeal of 10 U.S.C. 1599e (DoD probationary period)
rubrics_metrics.description: §752.401(c)(2)(ii) is revised to reflect repeal of 10 U.S.C. 1599e effective December 31, 2022, restoring a 1-year probationary period (and reducing the alternative continuous service prong to 1 year) for covered Department of Defense employees, while clarifying that a 2-year probationary period applies to individuals hired prior to December 31, 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM interprets Public Law 117-81 to mean the statutory repeal applies only prospectively to those appointed on or after the effective date; regulatory text is amended to reflect transitional application and correct conforming language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions under 5 U.S.C. 7511(b)(1)-(3) are distinct categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress excluded three distinct types of political appointments from the definition of "employee" and adverse action rights under 5 U.S.C. 7511(b)(1)-(3): (1) high-level presidential appointees requiring Senate confirmation (PAS), (2) positions determined to be of confidential/policy character (the subject of this rule), and (3) other presidential appointees who do not require Senate confirmation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPM emphasizes these are separate statutory categories and its definitional change pertains specifically to the middle category (confidential/policy positions), not to the other categories.
